_**User**_

Phase: Specification. Using the documentation skill, create spec/requirements.md for a
Support Ticket Management System. No code.

Source requirements :
- Create a ticket; list tickets; view ticket details
- Update title, description, priority and assignee
- Add comments
- Search tickets by keyword; filter tickets by status
- Persist data in a database (data must survive restart)
- Validate input at the backend; display meaningful errors in the UI
- Backend-enforced state machine:
  OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED; OPEN → CANCELLED; IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED
  All other transitions rejected (e.g. CLOSED→OPEN, RESOLVED→OPEN, CANCELLED→OPEN)
- No secrets committed

Further requirements :
- Ticket fields: id, title (required, 3–200 chars), description (required, max 5000),
  priority (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL; default MEDIUM), status (always OPEN on creation,
  cannot be set on create), assignee (optional free-text name/email, max 100), createdAt, updatedAt
- Comments: author (required, max 100), body (required, 1–2000), createdAt; comments cannot be
  edited or deleted; comments allowed in any status
- CLOSED and CANCELLED are terminal: field updates are rejected; comments still allowed
- Status changes only via the status transition operation, never via the general field update
- Transition to the same status (e.g. OPEN→OPEN) is rejected
- Search: case-insensitive keyword match on title and description; can combine with status
  filter; results paginated, default sort createdAt descending
- Concurrent edits: optimistic locking; a stale update is rejected with a clear error
- Out of scope: authentication/authorisation, user management, attachments, notifications,
  deleting tickets

Structure the file as:
1. Purpose & Scope (incl. Out of Scope)
2. Glossary
3. Functional Requirements with IDs (FR-01...), each with acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then
   — include negative cases (validation failures, not found, invalid transition, terminal edits)
4. State machine requirement: full allowed-transition table and explicit rejected examples
5. Non-Functional Requirements (NFR-01...): persistence across restart, validation, error
   clarity, no secrets, testability, basic performance (pagination)
6. Traceability table: each assignment acceptance criterion → FR/NFR IDs
7. Open Questions: anything still ambiguous — list, don't decide
8. Change Log

Don't create any other spec files yet.

_**User**_

Update spec/requirements.md. Fixes needed:

1) Add FR-12 "User interface" with Given/When/Then ACs covering: create ticket from UI,
   list tickets, view details incl. comments, edit title/description/priority/assignee,
   add comment, keyword search, status filter, perform status transitions (UI offers only
   transitions valid for the current status, but backend remains the authority), and
   display backend errors: field-level validation messages next to the fields, plus clear
   messages for not found, invalid transition, terminal-ticket edit, and stale version
   (prompt user to reload).

2) Add explicit ACs under FR-04 for assignee: change assignee to a new value; clear assignee
   (sending an empty string stores null); assignee change on terminal ticket rejected.

3) Add NFR-07 "State machine integration tests": automated integration tests run against the
   real API and a real PostgreSQL database (Testcontainers) covering every allowed transition
   and every disallowed transition in the full status × status matrix, including same-status;
   the build fails if any of them fail.

4) Replace the traceability table with two tables:
   a) "Assignment core acceptance criteria" — exactly these 15 rows, verbatim, each mapped to
      FR/NFR IDs: Ticket can be created from UI; Tickets can be listed; Ticket details can be
      viewed; Ticket fields can be updated; Assignee can be changed; Comments can be added;
      Search works; Status filter works; Valid status transitions work; Invalid status
      transitions are rejected by backend; Data survives application restart; Backend
      validation works; UI shows meaningful errors; State-machine integration tests pass;
      No secrets are committed.
   b) "Design decisions" — the additional rules (field limits, terminal behaviour, locking etc.)
      mapped to IDs.

5) Resolve the open questions with these decisions, update the affected ACs, and move them to a
   "Resolved Decisions" section (keep Open Questions empty unless new ones arise):
   1. Create payload containing status → rejected with 400 (unknown/forbidden fields rejected)
   2. Page size default 20, max 100; page numbering starts at 0
   3. Status filter accepts a single status value
   4. Comments shown in createdAt ascending order (chronological)
   5. Assignee is free text up to 100 chars; no email format validation
   6. Adding a comment does not require the ticket version
   7. Invalid status filter value → 400
   8. Field update is a partial update (PATCH): omitted fields unchanged; title/description/
      priority cannot be set to null; version is required in the request
   9. PostgreSQL via Docker Compose at runtime; Testcontainers PostgreSQL for integration tests;
      Flyway migrations (details belong in architecture.md)
   10. Error format is RFC 7807 Problem Details with a field errors array (details belong in
       api-contract.md)

6) Tidy FR-11: remove AC1 (it's not a verifiable outcome) and renumber.

7) Add a Change Log entry (0.2.0) summarising these changes.
